saturnus 0.12.0 teaches your AI app four more of the calculator's screens,
makes Files calmer while it works, and brings the Linux packages of
`saturnus` and `satx` to aarch64.

## Get it

- **On the web**, nothing to install: <https://ractive.ch/saturnus/app/>
  (Chrome, Edge or Firefox for a serial cable; every browser for the
  emulated calculator).
- **The desktop app** `saturnus_0.12.0_…` (on Linux `saturnus-app`), with
  a `-SHA256SUMS` file beside them:
  - macOS, Apple silicon: `.dmg`, signed and notarised, or `brew trust
    --cask ractive/tap/saturnus-app` once, then `brew install --cask
    ractive/tap/saturnus-app`;
  - Windows: `.msi` or `-setup.exe` for x86_64 (`x64`) and ARM (`arm64`);
  - Linux: `.deb`, `.rpm` or `.AppImage` for x86_64 (`amd64`, `x86_64`)
    and ARM (`arm64`, `aarch64`). Add yourself to the `dialout` group to
    use a serial port.
- **The command-line tools** `saturnus` and `satx`: `cargo install`,
  Homebrew `ractive/tap`, Scoop `ractive`, or the archives and Linux
  packages below.
- **Libraries** on crates.io, all at 0.12.0.

## Your AI

- **The EquationWriter on the 48SX and 48GX.** `screen` says "equation
  writer", or "equation view" for its scrolling mode (▼ on an algebraic,
  where ENTER does nothing), instead of "unknown", and `next` says how
  to leave without losing the formula. `to_stack` leaves the view for
  the EquationWriter and stops there. While it is open, `read_stack` no
  longer lists the EquationWriter's working objects as the stack.
- **The interactive stack, object edits and the MatrixWriter** on the
  48SX, 48GX and 49G. `screen` says "interactive stack" (▲ at the stack,
  the 49G's HIST), "object edit" (an object put on the command line by
  ▼, EDIT or VISIT) and "matrix writer" (also while a cell is typed)
  instead of "unknown" or "program input", each with its own `next`.
  `to_stack` leaves the interactive stack; it presses nothing in an
  object edit or the MatrixWriter, where CANCEL drops changes.
  `read_stack` and the display say when an object is off the stack
  while it is edited.
- **The question before storing or purging a variable** shows invisible
  characters in the arguments and in the AI app's name as `\uXXXX`.
- **"Allow until reload"** replaces "Always allow" in that question, left
  of Allow. A tool that may ask you says so to the AI app, and the tools
  describe their results.
- **The AI's calls note each reconnect attempt** ("Try 1 failed. Next
  try in 10 s"). Disconnect in the connect dialog says why when the
  relay refused it or did not answer.

## Files

- **A running transfer is shown once.** The rows being copied keep their
  thin bar, and the head of the calculator's (or palmtop's) pane says
  the job beside a spinner, for example "Copying ZPAR… 2 of 3", with
  Stop where the job can be stopped.
- **The Transfers list appears only when it has something to add:**
  several jobs under way, or a failed one. A failed job stays there,
  with what went wrong, until you dismiss it.
- **Reading a directory is said once,** in the pane's status ("Reading
  HOME…") with a spinner in the list. With reduced motion the spinner
  stands still.
- **No flash after a copy.** When a file arrives in the directory shown,
  or you rename or refresh it, the rows stay until the new listing
  replaces them. The tree keeps its folders while it reads a directory
  again.
- **"Files in this browser" explains itself.** An ⓘ beside the name says
  where the files are (the browser's own storage, not your disk), how
  they come in and go out, how long they stay, and why there is no
  folder in Firefox and Safari.
- **The palmtop reconnects by itself.** After you end the session on an
  HP 100LX or 200LX and come back to Filer, the next step in Files, such
  as Refresh, connects again and carries on instead of failing with "The
  palmtop stopped answering". The setup steps also say not to press
  Remote (F6).

## Linux packages for aarch64

- The .deb and .rpm of `saturnus` and `satx` now come for aarch64 too
  (`saturnus-v0.12.0-aarch64-linux.deb` and `.rpm`, and satx's
  likewise), with the same static binary as the archives.
- Every package has a build provenance attestation
  (`gh attestation verify <file> --repo ractive/saturnus`).

## Smaller changes

- Built with Rust 1.100; dependencies updated.
